## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5b88fd4081e7aea95e8779e30719ef4e309dfc5a`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed against card #16056 (body and all six comments, ruling `5564448371`), PR #20985 (body, file list, net diff `origin/main...5b88fd408`: 1 file, +4 / −0), the 36 check-runs on the head, and `origin/main` at `05be3525` (`AGENTS.md` Documentation Guardrails, `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts`, `packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`, the release pages, and the `@objectstack/cli@17.3.0` / `17.4.0` / `17.5.0` tags read with `git show`). Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff adds four lines to `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx` (:649–652) under the `os migrate meta --from 17` upgrade bullet. No accept set and no public surface moves; every judgment below is about the truth and form of published release text.

1. **Form against the ruling — RIGHT.** The line is dated (`2026-10-01`, the head commit's UTC day), referenced (#15585, #16058), appended in place as a continuation of the bullet's own paragraph, and the original sentence is byte-identical (`main:648` unchanged; 0 lines removed). It states what the command prints and what the 17.3.0 output was, which is the shape the ruling fixes.
2. **Right page, right bullet — RIGHT.** The card's `v17.mdx:5363` moved when the page was split per release; `runtime 17.0.0` has exactly one hit under `content/` on `main`, `17-3.mdx:648`, inside `### 17.3.0` → "Getting onto the release". The correction sits under that sentence and nowhere else.
3. **Dedicated docs-only PR — RIGHT.** One file under `content/docs/releases/`, no code, no `CHANGELOG.md`, no `.changeset`. This is the "dedicated docs-only PR" the `AGENTS.md` Documentation Guardrails row for `content/docs/releases/` names, not a rider.
4. **The quoted text, verbatim — RIGHT in spacing and label.** `meta.ts:627` on `main` prints `Chain:  protocol ${fromMajor} → ${toMajor} (this runtime implements protocol ${PROTOCOL_MAJOR})` through `printInfo`, which prefixes only `  ℹ `. Two spaces after `Chain:`, the U+2192 arrow and `PROTOCOL_MAJOR = 17` all match the line as quoted; the dev was right to keep the two spaces the ruling text collapsed to one.
5. **"`runtime 17.0.0` was the 17.3.0 output" — RIGHT.** At tag `@objectstack/cli@17.3.0`, `meta.ts:353` prints `(runtime ${PROTOCOL_VERSION})` and `@objectstack/spec@17.3.0` has `PROTOCOL_VERSION = '17.0.0'`. The remote tags carry no `cli@17.3.x` between 17.3.0 and 17.4.0.
6. **"from 17.4.0" as the first build — RIGHT.** #16058's merge `135843d` is an ancestor of `cli@17.4.0` and not of `cli@17.3.0`; `packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md` first carries the line under `## 17.4.0` (:4743–4751). At that tag `meta.ts:366` prints the new template and `toMajor = flags.to ?? PROTOCOL_MAJOR` (:288), so `--from 17` printed `17 → 17`; the 17.4.0 e2e test (:509–511) asserted exactly that for an unpinned `--from 17`.
7. **"from 17.4.0 the command prints `Chain:  protocol 17 → 17 (this runtime implements protocol 17)`" as a claim about every build from 17.4.0 on — WRONG, and this is the verdict.** The bullet's command is `os migrate meta --from 17` with no `--to`. In 17.5.0 (`fb39b38`, #17462: an ancestor of `cli@17.5.0`, not of `cli@17.4.0`; `packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md` `## 17.5.0` :1030–1040) `--to` began defaulting to `CHAIN_TERMINUS_MAJOR = Math.max(PROTOCOL_MAJOR, ...MIGRATION_MAJORS)` (`meta.ts:88`, `:544` on `main`), and the registry carries a major-18 step (`registry.ts:18923–18926`, already at `spec@17.4.0`). So on 17.5.0 and on `origin/main` that command prints `Chain:  protocol 17 → 18 (this runtime implements protocol 17)`. The repo says so in three places: the e2e test on `main` pins `--to` to `PROTOCOL_MAJOR` precisely because the unqualified default "is designed to drift" (`migrate-meta.e2e.test.ts:502–512`); the 17.5.0 page records that the command "now defaults `--to` to the highest registered major and lists the protocol-18 edits" (`17-5.mdx:149–156`, `:1720–1723`); and the 17.5.0 changelog entry is titled for it. The correction is therefore true of 17.4.0 alone and false of the current release and of `main`: a reader on 17.5.0 who runs the bullet's command gets `17 → 18` and is told, in a line dated today, to expect `17 → 17`. That is the "page describes a build that is not yours" defect this card was filed to remove, re-introduced in the sentence meant to remove it. The PR body's "The printed line this bullet describes is identical in 17.4.0 and 17.5.0" is wrong: the source template is identical, the printed line is not, because its `toMajor` half moved. Under the ruling, published release text is never silently rewritten, so once merged this line could only be repaired by a second dated correction beneath it; the cost of landing it wrong is permanent, which is why this is a FAIL and not a note. A true line is the dev's to word within the ruled form (dated, referenced, in place, original untouched): either quote the 17.4.0 output and say that from 17.5.0 the `→ 17` end is the registry's highest major (18, #17462), or state only the parenthetical's change (`(runtime 17.0.0)` → `(this runtime implements protocol 17)`) without asserting the chain ends. Either way, the line must be measured against the build on `main`, not only the 17.3.0 and 17.4.0 tarballs.
8. **Citations — RIGHT.** #15585 (closed completed 2026-09-10) and #16058 (merged 2026-09-06, "Part of #15585", lands the human-readable line) both resolve, and "the human-readable line landed in #16058" is accurate. The line does not cite #16056 itself; the sibling precedent (#16122 → PR #16493) cites both the fix and the card, but the ruling's own template for this card names #15585 only, so no finding.
9. **Check-runs on the head — read, and silent on the defect.** 36 runs: 26 `success`, 10 `skipped`, 0 failed, 0 pending; the one commit status (Vercel) is `success`. `Build Docs`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check Changeset`, `Type Check · workspace` are all green. No gate reads the semantic truth of a release-page sentence, so the green board does not contradict ①-7.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: no` — RIGHT.** The PR body and the claim comment both declare it. Nothing is published from any released package: no `package.json` `files[]` on `main` ships `content/docs`, and no accept set or public surface moves.
- **`skip-changeset` — RIGHT.** `AGENTS.md` Post-Task Checklist step 3 reserves that label for "a diff that publishes nothing from any released package", which this is. `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head.
- **The ruling's "rides the changeset into the next release's notes" half — not owed by this PR, as the dev claims.** The precedent agrees: the sibling #16122 correction landed as PR #16493 (`8d0aede6c9`) with two `CHANGELOG.md` files and no `.changeset`. The fact this correction records already rode #16058's and #17261's changesets into published notes (`packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md` 17.4.0 :4743–4751 and 17.5.0 :1072; `packages/metadata-core/CHANGELOG.md:278`; `17-5.mdx:1710–1711`). One consequence worth stating: the next release's notes will inherit whatever this line says, which is one more reason to land it true (①-7).

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report: `os-dev-report` comment `5922099669`. `open_questions` is empty; nothing to answer there.

Deviations:

1. *Two spaces after `Chain:` where the ruling spells one* — answered, accepted: two spaces is what `meta.ts:627` prints on `main` and at the 17.4.0 and 17.5.0 tags; the ruling text collapsed the spacing, the code did not.
2. *"from 17.4.0" instead of "from the build carrying #15585", citing #16058 beside #15585* — answered in two halves. As a lower bound and as a citation it is right (①-6, ①-8). As an open-ended range it is the FAIL in ①-7: the dev measured the 17.3.0 and 17.4.0 tarballs and, by the report's own account, read 17.5.0 only for the `--json` key rename, so the claim that the printed line is "identical in 17.4.0 and 17.5.0" was never measured for the bullet's own invocation. The ruling's literal `17 → 17` was written on 2026-09-07, before 17.5.0 (2026-09-29) moved the `--to` default; its *form* binds, and its template's facts were true when ruled. The dev already took the licence to restate the ruling's template in measured terms; the same licence obliges measuring every build the restated range names. Escalation path, only if needed: if the dispatching seat reads the ruling's `17 → 17` literal as binding verbatim even where the current release prints otherwise, that is a re-ruling question for the maintainer under the same batch-#65 rule, not something a reviewer can PASS over.
3. *Date moved to 2026-10-01 in a second commit* — accepted; the net diff against the merge base is still +4 / −0 and the date is the authoring day.
4. *Model-free commit trailers instead of the harness line* — accepted; `AGENTS.md:453–456` is the rule, both commits carry `Claude-Session:` + `Co-authored-by: Claude`, and no model identifier appears in the PR, the commits or the report.
5. *Built the `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/client-react` closures so two derived gates could record a verdict* — a dev-side build, not a review concern; the head's `Lint & Repo Gates` and type-check runs cover the same families and are green. Accepted.
6. *One malformed MCP read, no data, no effect* — accepted.

`out_of_scope_findings`:

- *`17-4.mdx` carries no line for the #16058 repair* — confirmed on `main` (`17-4.mdx:627–631` has the bullet; nothing names the chain line). Release-owned, carrier none; correct not to touch here. Stays noted.
- *17.3.0 and 17.4.0 `--json` still carry `runtime: "17.0.0"`* — confirmed (`cli@17.4.0` `meta.ts:335`; renamed to `protocolVersion` in 17.5.0 by #17261, `cca1dc0`). Outside this bullet, which is about the printed line only. Stays noted.

Reviewer's own flag, carrier none: the bullet's headline ("Expect `os migrate meta --from 17` to report `Nothing to migrate`") is also no longer what 17.5.0 does (`17-5.mdx:1720–1723`), for the same #17462 reason as ①-7. That is the historical reading and the 17.5.0 page records its own behaviour, so it is not this card's scope; it is named here so the re-worded correction does not accidentally assert it either.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-16056-v17-3-correction-line`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JAhu8u8QfBvRjVZDox7CP9`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
